explanation: Baseline feedback shows a successful fit (mse ~0.0313, nmse ~0.1907) with 8 declared parameters. The only observed evidence is a working but restricted feature set: one bilinear term (u0*u1) and no quadratic or other cross terms, so any curvature in u0*u2, u1*u2, or pure quadratics is left unexplained and acts as structured residual. I therefore keep the exact same signature, input order, parameter-index linear structure (bounded least squares from ones), and scaling envelope, and add six strictly linear-in-parameter basis terms (c8..c13) spanning the missing pair products and self-quadratics inside the same scaled envelope. This preserves the well-conditioned 'core * (1+c1 u0)(1+c2 u1)(1+c2 u2)' form that already fits, while enlarging the span so the residual curvature can be absorbed, raising the declared count from 8 to 14. Output remains a finite float64 array of shape (len(u0),) via nan_to_num, with no I/O, files, or extra packages. Indices are guarded so any n_params from 0..16 yields valid behavior. Trade-off accepted: 6 more parameters for a larger linear-in-params span; if the added terms are not needed the bounded least-squares fit simply drives their weights toward zero.
